summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease, chronic pain, and long-term steroid use was admitted with severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea after eating sausage patties, initially concerning for a flare or infection. He was dehydrated with acute kidney injury (creatinine 2.0, baseline 1.1) and leukocytosis. Stool studies were negative for pathogens, and renal ultrasound showed no hydronephrosis. Management included IV fluids, bowel rest, increased prednisone to 40 mg, a 10-day course of ciprofloxacin, and continuation of pain medications including Lyrica and tizanidine. His renal function improved, leukocytosis resolved, and he tolerated advancing diet. He received a vitamin B12 injection and was discharged home with a prednisone taper, calcium/vitamin D supplementation, and follow-up arranged with gastroenterology and pain clinic.
